capture.hash_scope: SHA-256 of normalized visible excerpts only, not raw HTTP response bytes.
capture.limitation: SEC pages and PDFs were read as rendered public documents. No raw HTTP body archive or exact per-request retrieval timestamp was captured.
capture.copyright_note: Source preservation uses short identifying excerpts (within quotation limits) plus original paraphrased summaries; hashes cover the short excerpts, not raw HTTP bytes.

key_findings: The SEC/CFTC Commission-level interpretive release S7-2026-09, effective 2026-03-23, explicitly lists XRP among digital commodities based on the Commission's understanding of its characteristics, terms and functions as of the release date.

The interpretation says digital commodities are not themselves securities, but a non-security crypto asset can still be offered or sold subject to an investment contract. Asset classification does not immunize every issuer, promoter, offering or transaction.

SEC Division of Corporation Finance FAQs were updated 2026-11-02. The SEC page explicitly says they are staff views, not a rule or Commission statement, and have no legal force or effect. They clarify that functional and decentralized are distinct and that decentralization depends on operational, economic and voting control.

The separate Regulation Crypto Assets proposal S7-2026-27 remains labelled Proposed on the SEC page after its 2026-10-20 comment deadline. The proposal is not an effective exemption. The SEC public docket shows additional post-deadline comments and meeting memoranda through 2026-11-05; docket activity is not adoption.

John Reed Stark and Lee Reiners filed an opposition letter on 2026-10-16 urging withdrawal and arguing the proposal conflicts with judicial precedent, including Ripple. This is a commenter position, not the SEC's conclusion or a court ruling.
The Senate's 2026-09-15 cloture vote on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 failed 49-50. The bill did not advance on that vote; this is not a final enactment.

commission_interpretation.classification_basis: Based on characteristics, terms and functions as of the date of the release; linked to the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system and supply/demand dynamics.
commission_interpretation.legal_scope: The Commission interpretation says digital commodities are not themselves securities. It also expressly states that a non-security crypto asset can be offered and sold subject to an investment contract, which is a security.
not_established: That every XRP sale or distribution is outside securities laws.
That every Ripple product, financing, custody or institutional arrangement is exempt.
That the interpretation is legislation or cannot be revised, challenged or applied differently to later facts.

staff_faq.explicit_disclaimer: The SEC page says the FAQs are not a rule, regulation or Commission statement, and have no legal force or effect.
staff_faq.clarification: Functional and decentralized are distinct. Functional concerns use of the native asset according to programmatic utility. Decentralized concerns autonomous operation without a person, entity or group having operational, economic or voting control.
staff_faq.xrp_specific_effect: No new XRP-specific reclassification was identified in the Nov 2 FAQ. It provides general interpretive context only.

central_party_test.summary: The SEC staff FAQ describes a central party as one with operational, economic or voting control. Relevant facts include authority over access at protocol, validator or user level; validator participation or consensus; upgrade/voting processes; and rule changes or transaction reversals. Broad-based governance participants generally are not a group when unaffiliated and not acting in concert.
research_requirements: Map Ripple's direct or indirect influence over validator lists, validator participation, consensus, software upgrades, governance and access.
Separate Ripple Labs, XRPL Foundation, independent validators, XRP holders, exchanges and application operators.
Do not infer central-party status from inventory holdings, business relationships or public advocacy alone.

terms: Proposed exemption for offerings up to $5 million over four years.
Proposed exemption for offerings up to $75 million in each 12-month period.
Principles-based disclosures, continuing antifraud/antimanipulation provisions and a conditional investment-contract safe harbor.

proposed_rule.interpretation: Post-deadline docket additions do not extend the stated comment deadline or prove adoption. The SEC rule page still labels the item Proposed.

counter_positions.position: Oppose and withdraw proposed Regulation Crypto Assets.
argument_scope: Proposal conflicts with parts of the judicial record and prior SEC positions.
Proposal's offering exemptions and safe harbor may exceed statutory authority.
Ripple case is discussed as part of the judicial record.
counter_positions.self_reported_independence: The authors state they hold no crypto positions, represent no crypto clients and derive no revenue dependent on the rulemaking outcome.

legislative_context.bill: H.R. 3633, Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025
legislative_context.implication: The bill did not advance on that procedural vote; do not describe it as enacted or as a final merits rejection.

event_timeline.event: Interpretive release effective; XRP explicitly listed as a digital commodity.
Senate cloture on motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 not invoked, 49-50.
SEC Corporation Finance staff FAQs updated.
SEC docket lists a meeting memorandum dated Nov 5 for a Nov 4 meeting.

source_registry.summary: The Commission's digital-commodity examples explicitly include XRP.
The release distinguishes an asset's classification from a particular offer or sale; a non-security asset can still be subject to an investment contract.
The FAQs are nonbinding staff views. They explain functionality, decentralization and central-party control as separate fact-specific questions.
The proposal contains two offering exemptions and a conditional safe harbor but remains proposed and not effective.
The docket records post-deadline comments and meeting memoranda through Nov 5; these filings do not establish adoption.

source_registry.publisher: John Reed Stark and Lee Reiners
source_registry.normalized_excerpt: in opposition to the Commission's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets
source_registry.summary: The authors urge withdrawal and argue the proposal conflicts with legal precedent; this is advocacy, not an SEC finding or court holding.
Cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 was not invoked; the bill did not advance on that procedural vote.

claims_supported: Senate procedural vote was 49-50 and the bill did not advance.
source_registry.limitation: Senate roll call is the primary vote source.

source_independence.disagreement: The Commission interpretation's favorable asset-level classification and the Stark/Reiners critique of the later proposed offering regime are different legal questions and different source positions; do not collapse them into a single 'SEC says XRP is safe' conclusion.
source_independence.independence_rule: The comment letter is not independent proof of its legal conclusions. The SEC docket is authoritative for filings and dates; the Senate roll call is authoritative for the procedural vote.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The Commission's explicit digital-commodity classification reduces baseline U.S. uncertainty around XRP as an asset.
supporting: XRP is named in the Commission-level interpretive release effective March 23, 2026.
disconfirming: Classification is based on characteristics as of the release date and is not legislation.
Specific offers, sales or arrangements can still be investment contracts.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Transaction-specific securities exposure remains possible even when XRP itself is classified as a digital commodity.
supporting: The Commission release expressly preserves investment-contract analysis for non-security crypto assets.
The SEC staff FAQ addresses representations, central parties and facts-and-circumstances analysis.
disconfirming: The Commission's current interpretation provides a clearer asset-level taxonomy than the earlier enforcement-only posture.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The proposed offering regime may face legal and political obstacles before becoming effective.
supporting: The SEC docket still labels S7-2026-27 Proposed.
Stark/Reiners filed a detailed opposition letter.
disconfirming: The SEC may still adopt a revised rule under its existing authority; the comment letter is advocacy, not a ruling.

model_ineligibility_reasons: Legal status is an event/context feature, not a directional price signal by itself.
No point-in-time market-response study or out-of-sample event study was completed.
The proposed rule is unresolved and the legal effects remain transaction-specific.
